definitions: A bias that arises in any study when individuals select themselves into a group, causing a biased sample with non-random distribution of characteristics.
A type of bias where the participants in a study are not randomly chosen but rather choose to participate, leading to a sample that may not be representative of the larger population.
examples: The survey results were skewed due to Self-Selection Bias.
Researchers must account for Self-Selection Bias in observational studies.
Self-Selection Bias can invalidate conclusions if not addressed.
